steps.body: Every subtraction is an addition fact read backwards. 13 − 5 asks: 5 and what make 13?
steps.narration: Every subtraction is an addition fact read backwards. 13 − 5 asks: 5 and what make 13?

widget.prompt: Start at 5 and hop forward until you reach 13.

commonLandings.feedback: That lands short of 13. Keep hopping until you arrive exactly.
That stays at the starting point. Hop forward until 13 is reached.

widget.missFeedback: Start at 5 and make 8 hops right, one number at a time.
widget.successFeedback: Eight hops on from 5 reaches 13, so 13 − 5 = 8.

predict.reveal: Subtraction asks for the missing part: 5 + 8 = 13, so 13 − 5 = 8. Reversing it to "13 and what make 5?" breaks — 13 is already past 5, so no counting number can be added to reach it.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g2f think addition.
invariants: The manipulated model and the mathematical relationship for g2f think addition must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Changing a visible feature without preserving the relationship that defines g2f think addition.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same mathematical relationship?

explanationVariants: Every subtraction is an addition fact read backwards.

commonErrors.feedback: That repeats the total. The question asks what is LEFT after 5 comes off.
That repeats the part taken away instead of the part remaining.
